spec.joins: churn rows from run_midmonth(full_churn=True) joined by decision date against panel_screen.split_events on the raw prints
spec.hit_window: event date d counts when decision date < d <= next decision date
spec.why_this_cost_set: the churn sleeve is a name-level mean, not a portfolio return, so no cost multiplier can move it; the standard triple is kept so the sleeve lands beside the turnover control of the same burn

honest: a hit transition says a print event sits inside the priced window; it does not say the book traded that name on that bar
the churn sleeve is an equal-weight mean over the swapped names, so a single large print can move one transition's alpha by more than a clean year
drop mode removes names entirely, so its delta mixes repair with composition and is not comparable cell-for-cell with the neutralise arms
transitions are counted, not weighted: a period with more rebalances contributes more rows, and the era means are unweighted
the event index comes from the raw prints, so a name that never traded a suspicious bar is clean by construction and cannot explain anything here
descriptive census only: no gate, no verdict, no prereg, no trial booking
